Full Admission Information › Entrances, Directions & Parking › Seasonal Hours September Tuesday–Thursday: 10 a.m.–7 p.m. Friday–Sunday: 10 a.m.–6 p.m. Members’ Fall Mornings : Saturday & Sunday, 9–10 a.m. beginning September 12 Closed Mondays October Tuesday–Sunday: 10 a.m.–6 p.m. Special tickets needed: Saturday, October 24 for Fall Harvest Festival . No regular Garden admission on this day. Closed Mondays (except open October 12 , 10 a.m.–6 p.m.) Members’ Fall Mornings : Saturday & Sunday, 9–10 a.m. Admission All visitors must present ticket for entrance. Members and affiliates with free tickets must also show proof of eligibility. Advance tickets are recommended. Tickets are available 30 days in advance of visit dates. Same-day tickets may be obtained at Garden admission booths. Children under 12 are free. Children under 14 must be supervised by an adult 18 or over. Tickets are nonrefundable , but may be exchanged in advance of visit for another date. Ticket Prices Ticket Type Box Office Online Members Free Free Adults $22 $23.67 ($22 + $1.67 Fee) Seniors (65+) $16 $17.47 ($16 + $1.47 Fee) Students 12+ with ID $16 $17.47 ($16 + $1.47 Fee) Children under 12 Free Free Community tickets A portion of each day's tickets are available free of charge to those who need them. Supported by JPMorgan Chase. Museum & Garden Combo See below. Winter Weekdays (December–February) Pay what you wish. Get Tickets Become a Member Members receive free general admission every day. Museum & Garden Ticket Enhance your day in Brooklyn by visiting our neighbor, the Brooklyn Museum! Purchase a Museum & Garden ticket here at Brooklyn Botanic Garden and present your receipt for same-day admission to the Brooklyn Museum. Ticket Type Box Office Online Adults $34 $36.06 ($34 + $2.06 Fee) Seniors (65+) $24 $25.73 ($24 + $1.73 Fee) Students (20+) $24 $25.73 ($24 + $1.73 Fee) Students (12–19) $16 $17.47 ($16 + $1.47 Fee) Book Museum & Garden Tickets Restrictions Museum & Garden visits must be made on the same date. The Museum is closed on Tuesdays. Offer is not valid for special events. The Brooklyn Museum’s admission is suggested. Tickets are not refundable. There is no combination ticket for children under 12 years of age. Children under 12 enter for free. Your Support Makes Great Things Possible! Admissions and membership revenue helps Brooklyn Botanic Garden care for its 52 acres of grounds and conservatories and provide the environmental education programs, breathtaking botanical displays, exciting public events, and community greening efforts that have made the Garden a world-class living museum for all to enjoy. Thank you for supporting this with your visit! Free Admission Opportunities Admission is free: BBG members receive free general admission year-round. Children under 12 are always free. Community Tickets: A portion of each day’s tickets are available free of charge to those who need them. Pay-What-You-Wish Winter Weekdays: Tuesday–Friday, December–February Free admission during public hours is also offered to the individuals and groups listed below. Check full details at the link below before planning your visit. Academic members and participants in the following programs, with valid ID: Students, employees of Medgar Evers Students, employees, alum of Pratt Brooklyn Academy of Science and the Environment students and families, employees Cool Culture cardholders and their families Garden Apprentice Program teens and families Project Green Reach classrooms, students and families (with pass) Urban Advantage teachers, classrooms, students and families (with voucher) Visitors with the following affiliations, with valid ID: Individual members of the following museum and garden associations: AHS, APGA, Museums Council of New York City Members of gardens that participate in the AHS Reciprocal Admissions Program Employees of current corporate members Brooklyn Botanic Garden volunteers With preregistration: Public library patrons with a Culture Pass reservation (with pass) Registered, self-guided school and camp groups Registered, self-guided groups from nonprofit senior centers, shelters, rehabilitation centers, and other 501(c)(3) organizations serving people with disabilities Participants in accessibility programs, including monthly Memory Tours Community Greening & NYC Compost Project workshop participants Members of the press on assignment See Complimentary Admission Programs details › Entrances, Directions & Parking Entrances 150 Eastern Parkway is temporarily closed. 990 Washington Avenue Brooklyn, NY 11225 455 Flatbush Avenue Brooklyn, NY 11225 Public Transportation Subway to Eastern Parkway—Brooklyn Museum for 150 Eastern Parkway and 990 Washington Avenue entrances to Prospect Park for 455 Flatbush Avenue entrance (no B train on weekends) to Franklin Avenue (no elevator) for 990 Washington Avenue and 150 Eastern Parkway entrances Bus Nearest bus services: B16 to Ocean Avenue B41 to Empire Boulevard B43 to Washington Avenue B45 to Washington Avenue B48 to Eastern Parkway 10-minute walk from a Garden entrance: B16 to Lincoln Road B41 or B69 to Brooklyn Public Library B49 to Eastern Parkway B65 to Classon Avenue LIRR LIRR to Flatbush Avenue/Atlantic Avenue Station. Connect with 2, 3, 4, or 5 train or B41 bus. Parking Important: The parking lot is closed September 1–7 for West Indian American Day Carnival events and area parking is restricted. Taking public transportation to the Garden is recommended. Attended parking (for a fee) is available at 900 Washington Avenue. The parking lot is open from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. There is no overnight parking; monthly parking by arrangement. Time Rate (off-peak days) Up to 1 hour $10 Up to 2 hours $12 Up to 3 hours $14 Up to 4 hours $16 Up to 5 hours $18 Maximum to closing $24 Up to 24 hours $35 Lost ticket (pays per day) $35 Special event rates apply on busy days. School buses (only when space permits): $25 for maximum to closing; $50 for up to 24 hours; $50 per day for lost ticket. Regular buses: $90 for maximum to closing; $120 for up to 24 hours; $120 per day for lost ticket. All rates subject to change. pages.main_text: Search Visitor Guidelines & FAQ Skip to main content Visitor Guidelines & FAQ Frequently Asked Questions Tips for Peak-Season Visitors Spring is our busiest season and you should be prepared for crowds. Reserve tickets in advance to speed admission. At the entrance, look for the Have a Ticket line reserved for ticketholders. Please have your ticket out with barcode ready to scan. Members and affiliates should present program ID along with their ticket barcode on entry. Get Tickets Free Member Tickets If you do not have an advance ticket, you’ll need to purchase tickets or request free member or affiliate tickets at the box office. Look for the Need a Ticket line. Take advantage of extended hours during bloom season. To avoid crowds, visit midweek or before 10 a.m. on weekends. Take public transportation, walk, or bike to the Garden . On peak weekends especially, the parking lot fills up and street traffic is heavy. Please help care for our collections. Do not touch plants or shake tree branches. Deposit trash in an appropriate receptacle. Outside food and beverages are not permitted. An interactive map of the Garden is available at bbg.org/map . Visiting: What to See, When to Come, How Long to Stay How long does a visit take? Seeing the entire Garden would take a full day. There are suggested itineraries for shorter visits. What is in bloom right now? When are the cherry trees in bloom? The Plants in Bloom page will tell you! The cherry trees typically bloom throughout April and early May. CherryWatch provides frequent updates in the spring. Are you ever open in the evening? Yes, the Garden is open late on select days in peak season. For details, see our Hours & Admission page. Also, if you are a member , you can attend Members’ Summer Evenings on Wednesdays, 6–8:30 p.m. Tickets & Entry Do I need a ticket? All visitors, including children and members, need a ticket to enter. Garden members and members of affiliated organizations will show their program ID with their free ticket on entry. Tickets may be purchased at each entrance or online at bbg.org/tickets . Online tickets are available 30 days in advance. If you are feeling unwell, please postpone your visit. Use the “cancel my tickets” link on your confirmation or contact our ticketing partner Leap at 866-220-4001 to reschedule your visit. Unused tickets cannot be exchanged after the visit date. There are no refunds. Where is the entrance? Public entrances are located at: 455 Flatbush Avenue 990 Washington Avenue Our 150 Eastern Parkway entrance is currently closed. Purchase tickets at the admission booth or have your tickets ready for scanning. Please review visitor guidelines ; there is not a checkroom for items that are not allowed on the grounds. See Hours & Admission for seasonal hours. Last entry is 30 minutes before the Garden closes. Specialty gardens begin to close at this time. Rules What rules must all visitors follow? While visiting this museum of plants, please follow the Garden’s rules. Please don’t touch plants, pick flowers or other plant parts, climb trees, or walk in plant beds. Do not feed wildlife or release animals in the Garden. Pets and emotional support animals are not permitted in the Garden. Service animals are always welcome. No athletics or recreational equipment. Jogging, scooters, balls, etc. are not allowed in the Garden. Do not smoke or vape in the Garden. Children under 14 must be supervised by an adult. No outside food and beverages; please consume items purchased on-site in designated areas. (Bottled water, baby bottles, and pocket snacks for individuals with dietary restrictions are allowed.) Sitting on the grass is permitted on Cherry Esplanade and in the Discovery Garden, Osborne Garden, Plant Family Collection, and Water Garden. Please see map for details. No blankets or folding chairs, please. Shirt and shoes are required. Use earphones for all electronic audio devices. Tripods and easels are not permitted in the Japanese Hill-and-Pond Garden, the Conservatory, or flower beds. Please do not block paths. Drones are not permitted. Commercial and portrait photography is only allowed by prior arrangement. Visit bbg.org/photography to request a permit. Activities at Brooklyn Botanic Garden may be photographed and/or recorded. Your presence in the Garden constitutes your permission and authorization for use of your likeness and voice for Garden purposes. If you do not wish to be recorded, you may inform the photographer. Please read through the rest of these FAQ and other areas of the website for more detailed information on specific rules and policy, and be considerate of others during your visit. If you have any questions about these rules, contact [email protected] . Entry into the Garden constitutes consent by the visitor to follow all Garden rules and to accept direction from the Security team. The Garden reserves the right to deny entry to or escort from the grounds any individuals or groups acting in ways deemed harmful to the Garden or that impinge upon the enjoyment of the Garden by other guests. Garden Etiquette: Picnics, Strollers, Bikes, Pets, Tree Climbing, Smoking Can we bring a picnic? May we sit on the lawn? Picnicking is not allowed at BBG. Sitting on the lawn is permitted on Cherry Esplanade and in the Discovery Garden, Osborne Garden, Water Garden, and Plant Family Collection. Are strollers allowed? Strollers are allowed on the grounds and in the Visitor Center, but not in the Steinhardt Conservatory or Terrain. Are scooters, bikes, roller skates, or skateboards allowed? No. There is no checkroom available and skates, skateboards, and scooters are not permitted. Bike racks are located near all entrances. Are pets allowed in the Garden? What about service animals? Pets are not allowed, but service animals are. Our accessibility guidelines provide more details. May we climb the trees? May we pick flowers and vegetables? Tree climbing is not allowed in order to keep both the trees and visitors safe. Please don’t pick flowers or vegetables. Edible food from our Herb Garden and display gardens is donated to local charities. Is smoking allowed? No, smoking is prohibited throughout the Garden. Access Is the entire Garden accessible to people with disabilities? All of our entrances and most of our pathways are accessible to people using wheelchairs and those with other disabilities. Certain paths may be uneven or steep. Please see our accessibility guidelines for more information. Amenities: Bathrooms, Food, Lockers, Plants and Merchandise for Sale Where can I buy food? Visitors to the Garden can enjoy modern, vegetable-focused cuisine in a full-service setting at Yellow Magnolia Café , casual entrées at the seasonal outdoor eatery Yellow Magnolia Canteen , or sandwiches, snacks, and drinks at the Coffee Bar at the Visitor Center. Please see map for details. Where are the bathrooms? There are bathrooms in the Visitor Center, at the Flatbush Avenue entrance, on Magnolia Plaza, in the Conservatory, outside Yellow Magnolia Café, and on Lily Pool Terrace. Please see map for locations. Do you sell plants? Yes, the retail shop Terrain has a selection of plants for sale. Do you have daily lockers or a coat check? No. Photography Can I take photographs? Can a professional photographer shoot my portrait? In general, visitors may take nonprofessional photos for personal use. Professional photographers must adhere to our photography policy. Can BBG be used for a commercial photo or film shoot? Yes, but you must receive prior approval. Please see our commercial and editorial photography guidelines for details. Weddings, Private Events, and Space Rental Can we get married at the Garden? Can I rent space for other events? Yes. Please see our Weddings and Celebrations and Private and Corporate Events pages for details. Field Trips: Schools and Camps I’m a teacher/camp counselor. Can I bring my students on a self-guided field trip? School and camp group visits are available free of charge by advance registration only. Learn more. Image, top of page: Michael Stewart

passages.text: Our 150 Eastern Parkway entrance is currently closed.

passages.heading: Where is the entrance?
passages.text: Purchase tickets at the admission booth or have your tickets ready for scanning. Please review visitor guidelines ; there is not a checkroom for items that are not allowed on the grounds.

passages.heading: Where is the entrance?
passages.text: See Hours & Admission for seasonal hours. Last entry is 30 minutes before the Garden closes. Specialty gardens begin to close at this time.

passages.heading: Rules
passages.text: What rules must all visitors follow?

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: While visiting this museum of plants, please follow the Garden’s rules.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Please don’t touch plants, pick flowers or other plant parts, climb trees, or walk in plant beds.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Do not feed wildlife or release animals in the Garden.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Pets and emotional support animals are not permitted in the Garden. Service animals are always welcome.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: No athletics or recreational equipment. Jogging, scooters, balls, etc. are not allowed in the Garden.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Do not smoke or vape in the Garden.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Children under 14 must be supervised by an adult.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: No outside food and beverages; please consume items purchased on-site in designated areas. (Bottled water, baby bottles, and pocket snacks for individuals with dietary restrictions are allowed.)

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Sitting on the grass is permitted on Cherry Esplanade and in the Discovery Garden, Osborne Garden, Plant Family Collection, and Water Garden. Please see map for details.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: No blankets or folding chairs, please.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Use earphones for all electronic audio devices.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Tripods and easels are not permitted in the Japanese Hill-and-Pond Garden, the Conservatory, or flower beds. Please do not block paths. Drones are not permitted.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Commercial and portrait photography is only allowed by prior arrangement. Visit bbg.org/photography to request a permit.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Activities at Brooklyn Botanic Garden may be photographed and/or recorded. Your presence in the Garden constitutes your permission and authorization for use of your likeness and voice for Garden purposes. If you do not wish to be recorded, you may inform the photographer.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Please read through the rest of these FAQ and other areas of the website for more detailed information on specific rules and policy, and be considerate of others during your visit. If you have any questions about these rules, contact [email protected] .

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?
passages.text: Entry into the Garden constitutes consent by the visitor to follow all Garden rules and to accept direction from the Security team. The Garden reserves the right to deny entry to or escort from the grounds any individuals or groups acting in ways deemed harmful to the Garden or that impinge upon the enjoyment of the Garden by other guests.

passages.heading: What rules must all visitors follow?

passages.heading: Garden Etiquette: Picnics, Strollers, Bikes, Pets, Tree Climbing, Smoking
passages.text: Can we bring a picnic? May we sit on the lawn?

passages.heading: Can we bring a picnic? May we sit on the lawn?
passages.text: Picnicking is not allowed at BBG. Sitting on the lawn is permitted on Cherry Esplanade and in the Discovery Garden, Osborne Garden, Water Garden, and Plant Family Collection.

passages.heading: Can we bring a picnic? May we sit on the lawn?
Are strollers allowed?
passages.text: Strollers are allowed on the grounds and in the Visitor Center, but not in the Steinhardt Conservatory or Terrain.

passages.heading: Are strollers allowed?
passages.text: Are scooters, bikes, roller skates, or skateboards allowed?

passages.heading: Are scooters, bikes, roller skates, or skateboards allowed?
passages.text: No. There is no checkroom available and skates, skateboards, and scooters are not permitted. Bike racks are located near all entrances.

passages.heading: Are scooters, bikes, roller skates, or skateboards allowed?
passages.text: Are pets allowed in the Garden? What about service animals?

passages.heading: Are pets allowed in the Garden? What about service animals?
passages.text: Pets are not allowed, but service animals are. Our accessibility guidelines provide more details.

passages.heading: Are pets allowed in the Garden? What about service animals?
passages.text: May we climb the trees? May we pick flowers and vegetables?

passages.heading: May we climb the trees? May we pick flowers and vegetables?
passages.text: Tree climbing is not allowed in order to keep both the trees and visitors safe. Please don’t pick flowers or vegetables. Edible food from our Herb Garden and display gardens is donated to local charities.

passages.heading: May we climb the trees? May we pick flowers and vegetables?
Is smoking allowed?
passages.text: No, smoking is prohibited throughout the Garden.

passages.heading: Access
passages.text: Is the entire Garden accessible to people with disabilities?

passages.heading: Is the entire Garden accessible to people with disabilities?
passages.text: All of our entrances and most of our pathways are accessible to people using wheelchairs and those with other disabilities. Certain paths may be uneven or steep. Please see our accessibility guidelines for more information.

passages.heading: Is the entire Garden accessible to people with disabilities?

passages.heading: Amenities: Bathrooms, Food, Lockers, Plants and Merchandise for Sale
Where can I buy food?
passages.text: Visitors to the Garden can enjoy modern, vegetable-focused cuisine in a full-service setting at Yellow Magnolia Café , casual entrées at the seasonal outdoor eatery Yellow Magnolia Canteen , or sandwiches, snacks, and drinks at the Coffee Bar at the Visitor Center. Please see map for details.

passages.heading: Where are the bathrooms?
passages.text: There are bathrooms in the Visitor Center, at the Flatbush Avenue entrance, on Magnolia Plaza, in the Conservatory, outside Yellow Magnolia Café, and on Lily Pool Terrace. Please see map for locations.

passages.heading: Do you sell plants?
passages.text: Yes, the retail shop Terrain has a selection of plants for sale.
